sonnet.problem: This true/false card says the LORD tells Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and the seventy elders to worship at a distance. That rules out the wrong answers 'Moses and Aaron' and 'Aaron alone' on card 5, and points straight to 'Moses alone'. A card that comes before a later choice card gives away its answer.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answers 'He pours it on the pillars' and 'He burns it on the altar' reuse 'pillars' and 'altar', which were already shown as answers on card 16. 'Altar' was card 16's right answer and 'pillars' was one of its wrong answers.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The true statement's first half ('The cloud covers Mount Sinai for six days') repeats what story card 12 just told ('For six days, the cloud covers it'). It also bundles two claims into one statement, so the card mostly repeats the card before it.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. ... A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The joke repeats the self-deprecating shape 'I can't do a small ordinary thing' that is already used in stop 1 card 7 (skipping to the oven temperature), stop 2 card 1 (winded hopping across the counter) and stop 2 card 3 (forgetting my own name). It is the same punchline shape a fourth time in the lesson.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
